keyVerseText: For Jozachar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.
rootMeaning: The name יְהוֹזָבָד (Yᵉhôwzâbâd) is derived from the Hebrew components יְהֹוָה (Jehovah) and זָבַד (to endow or bestow). Literally, it means "Jehovah has endowed," emphasizing that any gifts, strength, or authority associated with the bearers of this name are ultimately given by God. This etymology adds a profound layer beyond a mere personal name, highlighting divine provision and blessing as foundational to their identity.
usageInScripture: The name Jehozabad appears four times in Scripture, referring to three distinct individuals: a servant involved in the assassination of King Joash, a Benjamite military captain, and a Levitical porter in David's time. Translations consistently render the name as Jehozabad or with slight variations, underscoring its recognition as a proper name rather than a common noun. The consistency in translation reflects the importance of preserving the name's identity and its divine association across different contexts.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the meaning of Jehozabad as "Jehovah has endowed" reminds believers that all authority, service, and even personal identity are gifts from God. Whether the individual is a warrior, a temple porter, or even one involved in tragic events, their life and role are under God's sovereign provision. This reinforces the biblical truth that God equips His servants for their purposes, and His name within theirs serves as a testimony to His sustaining power. It prompts faithful reflection on how God’s endowment shapes our calling and actions in His kingdom.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 12:21, Jehozabad is named as one of the servants who struck down King Joash, leading to his death and the succession of Amaziah. The presence of this name in the verse highlights the human agents through whom divine judgment and historical events unfold. Knowing Jehozabad means "Jehovah has endowed" invites contemplation on how God's providence can work even through difficult and violent circumstances to fulfill His sovereign purposes in history.
